title: fix(state): keep quarantine refusals when reader cleanup fails
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes state and agent database admission losing a validated quarantine refusal when the quarantine metadata reader fails to close.

## User Impact

A database already known to be damaged remains refused through reader cleanup failure, and the error retains its cleanup cause for diagnosis. This repair requires no configuration change or operator action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The quarantine owner carries its validated decision through cleanup and supplies one refusal result to state and agent admission. State admission retains its separate native-cleanup fact. Cleanup-only agent failures remain retryable; known quarantine retains the integrity latch. Ordinary metadata failures keep their existing best-effort behavior.

The existing worker error format and conservative retirement wrapper preserve the cleanup lineage. Agent refusal precedes native source activation and the local opener's lease stage; already-held shared custody still waits for native termination or exit before release. This repair leaves the worker error format, schemas, permissions, and retention unchanged. Current main supplies its existing state-schema-18 migration; this PR adds no schema change.

The complete identity codec now owns error classification, identity validation, and construction in one sibling. The graph owner retains references, cycles, canonical admission, and per-caller hydration. This resolves the integration line-cap failure while preserving newer main's attachment-conflict identity and the native wrapper's eager closure. Raw-reader production test exports are removed; Doctor and verifier fixtures inspect persisted rows independently.

## Evidence

Private candidate `4f0305f71d2b975221b4f291e3e2f15656505880` integrates main `ca97ceb8f9bd712205da7fef9c65eb99c5cc6f45` while preserving the original PR ancestry and published `34cef992` ancestor. All 18 authored file patches are unchanged relative to main. Of the 16 authored code/test blobs, 15 are identical; the reply handler only inherited an extracted callback type. Its received-error cause, existing `currentError`, conservative outcome classification, and settlement ordering remain intact. The prior independent P2 review remains applicable after source qualification.

Main's retained-runtime repair in [#153764](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153764) captures worker generation before detached admission, keeps carriers within their generation, and joins accepted work and actual worker exit before removing retained code. Nine relevant owner/test blobs match that repair's independently recorded compiled proof exactly. That evidence retains its original source identity; it is not presented as execution of this PR.

Fresh [Blacksmith Testbox integration proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35715950233) used Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.4.0, four CPUs, and one test worker:

| Boundary | Passed cases | Wall seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Agent registration failures through retirement | 10 | 15.758 |
| Broker cleanup lineage and completed-write outcomes | 12 | 2.642 |
| Retained-generation capacity and unrelated workers | 1 | 17.922 |
| Native wrapper eager import closure | 14 | 19.168 |
| Emitted-worker typed errors and per-caller hydration | 3 selected | 22.209 |

All **40 selected cases passed**; 28 unrelated emitted-worker cases were intentionally filtered. The production `gatewayWatch` build passed in **58.215 s**, with all four relevant worker entries present and nonempty. Static JavaScript import closure passed in **17.093 s**.

The canonical emitted-artifact validator checked all **11,559 inputs and 15,547 outputs**. All **48,311 tracked source files**, **109 bound inputs**, and **17 downloaded artifacts** were verified; the source remained unchanged. The owned Testbox is stopped and independently confirmed completed. The Actions URL identifies the environment/lifecycle; native command receipts establish the results. Portal sync timed out after the successful workload, so no portal readback is claimed.

Preceding proof retains its original source identities: original-code controls reproduced refusal and cleanup-lineage loss; the 216-case source/sibling proof and static checks passed; subsequent scoped integrations passed 58 and 44 cases plus their build/import checks. These are reused only for unchanged contracts.

The [published-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35700053329) tested merge `1a19f5882f0ca9792b13e437259e98ac303b0664` on main `5c1c5077260ed54be07a30b66b6738cda2c57ff1`. All **155 cases in the eight changed test files passed**, and the authored patch plus its 82 bound inputs matched. Five other cases failed across three jobs: SQLite compile-cache child deadlines, an MCP import-boundary child deadline, and an approval-ordering setup assertion; the aggregate gate failed. Exact logs and original test groups remain retained.

Current main contains the canonical prepared-approval fixture repair [#155589](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155589), compile-cache setup repair `a3aa5390`, idle-coordinator lifecycle cleanup `6110505e`, maintenance-cache wrapper closure `b518db47`, and snapshot-loader imports `aeff5c8d`. The earlier failed CI already included `b1f107c1`; it is not claimed as a new fix. Passing replays do not establish the causes of the original failures. Fresh published-head CI has passed; native merge gates remain required.

<details>
<summary>Changed-test costs</summary>

Wall times below belong to the preceding 216-case private proof, using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. CI values are summed case durations from current head `4f0305f` at tested merge `c1a81d5d`; they exclude import, transform, setup, and worker startup. They are validation costs, not performance gains.

| File | Cases | Historical wall seconds | CI case seconds |

| `src/commands/doctor-state-sqlite-compact.test.ts` | 15 | 16.321 | 2.371 |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Retained failures and limits</summary>

Earlier CI's codec line-cap failure was repaired by the behavior-preserving identity extraction. Four historical Doctor test-body timeouts remained unexplained after one original-order 306-case replay passed. A previous Gateway `agent.wait` failure also remained unexplained: a 300-case diagnostic passed while exposing a separate inspection-cleanup warning. Main's canonical inspection-owner repair and lint follow-up address that warning; no causal claim is made about the original turn failure.

One approval-only diagnostic on the exact failed CI source passed all 482 cases across the original 23-file selection. It observed registration consuming 588 ms of the unchanged 2,000 ms deadline and durable resolution completing at 595 ms with `allowed` / `user`. Testbox resources were four CPUs and 16.56 GB versus the CI log's two CPUs and 8.22 GB; both used two workers. This is noncausal evidence. The separate canonical fixture repair moves real-worker preparation before the approval clock starts; this PR adds no competing fixture patch, deadline change, or authority exception.

Prior artifact-collector mistakes and a provider setup HTTP 429 are retained separately from successful command evidence. Proof covers injected cleanup faults, real emitted-worker typed-error flow, and static build/import closure. It does not inject a real native SQLite close failure or establish packaged/live Gateway behavior.

</details>

## Completed automated review

ClawSweeper completed its exact-head review with no actionable findings. Its generated migration-proof checkbox is rejected as a classifier false positive: error identity classification, validation, and construction relocate existing code; the runtime transport remains version 1; and cleanup aggregation changes no persisted schema, migrations, quarantine rows, retention, or configuration. The [review’s own technical evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152519#issuecomment-5739515356) explicitly retracts that requirement. The native source review remains ready; required CI and merge gates remain unchanged.

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35717893327) passed on attempt 1: 142 successful jobs, 15 intentional skips, and both required CI-gate results successful. All 155 cases in the eight changed test files passed. CI tested merge `c1a81d5d2ffb7f4c9406c6ad0334bcdbbf98294e` on main `45ba3419d63e27d5dff2845d44c184f30614b445`; the full authored patch is unchanged. The native review phases passed with zero findings, and the updated review records the migration-checklist refutation.
